label: df.multiple Eisenstein series
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{df.multiple Eisenstein series}
    Fix a positive integer $r$.
    For any $\mathbf{z}\in \Omega^r$ and nonempty index $\mathfrak{s} = (s_1,\ldots,s_m)$, we define the multiple Eisenstein series of rank $r$ by
    \[
    E_r(\mathfrak{s}; \mathbf{z}) = \sum_{\substack{\bm{f}_1,\ldots,\bm{f}_m \in A^r \\  \bm{f}_1\succ \cdots \succ  \bm{f}_m \succ 0}}\frac{1}{\left\langle \bm{f}_1,\mathbf{z}\right\rangle^{s_1}\cdots \left\langle \bm{f}_m, \mathbf{z}\right\rangle^{s_m}}.
    \]
    We adopt the convention that $E_r(\varnothing; \mathbf{z}): = 1$.

title: Remark
body_md: After completing the proofs of our main results, we learned that Bachmann and Kanno had posted on arXiv a paper proving \cref{Thm:BK26}. We then observed that their method could be adapted to strengthen our \cref{thm.main-thm} by replacing $\overline{K}$ with $\mathbb{C}_\infty$ when $r\geq 2$. Precisely, the proof of the first assertion in arbitrary rank and that of the second assertion in rank two follow a strategy similar to that of \cite{BK26}, while the second assertion in arbitrary rank is obtained by combining the rank two case with the induction argument used in the proof of \cref{thm.main-thm}. We refer to Appendix~\ref{appendix} for details.

label: df.partial order on Λ_z
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{df.partial order on Λ_z}
    For every nonzero
    $\bm{f}=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\in A^r$, we put
    \[
    \ell(\bm{f})
    :=
    \min\{i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\mid f_i\neq0\}.
    \]
    We define a partial order $\succ$ on $A^r$ as follows.
    For nonzero $\bm{f}\in A^r$, we write $\bm{f}\succ0$ if $f_{\ell(\bm{f})}\in A_+$.
    For $\bm{f},\bm{g}\succ0$, we write
    $\bm{f}\succ\bm{g}$
    if either
    $\ell(\bm{f})<\ell(\bm{g})$,
    or
    \[
    \ell(\bm{f})=\ell(\bm{g})
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \deg f_{\ell(\bm{f})}
    >
    \deg g_{\ell(\bm{g})}.
    \]

label: prop.ring of modular forms
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.ring of modular forms}
    For any integer $r\geq2$, the following assertions hold.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item (\cite[Proposition~15.12 and Proposition~16.3]{BBP24}) For $i=1,\ldots,r-1$, $g_i$ is a Drinfeld modular form of
        weight $q^i-1$, and $\Delta_r$ is a Drinfeld cusp form of weight
        $q^r-1$.
    
        \item (\cite[Theorem~17.5(a)]{BBP24}) We have
        \[
        \mathscr{M}^{(r)}
        =
        \mathbb{C}_\infty[g_1,\ldots,g_{r-1},\Delta_r],
        \]
        and $g_1,\ldots,g_{r-1},\Delta_r$ are algebraically independent
        over $\mathbb{C}_\infty$.
    
        \item (\cite[Theorem~17.5(a)]{BBP24}) We have
        \[
        \mathscr{M}^{(r)}
        =
        \mathbb{C}_\infty[
            E_{q-1}^{(r)},\ldots,E_{q^r-1}^{(r)}
        ],
        \]
        and $E_{q-1}^{(r)},\ldots,E_{q^r-1}^{(r)}$ are algebraically
        independent over $\mathbb{C}_\infty$, where, for $s\geq 1$ with
        $q-1\mid s$,
        \begin{equation}\label{eq.single Eisenstein series of weight a}
        E_s^{(r)}(\mathbf{z})
        =
        \sum_{0\neq\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}}}
        \frac{1}{\lambda^s}
        \end{equation}
        denotes the single Eisenstein series of rank $r$ and weight $s$.
    
        \item (\cite[Proposition~15.3]{BBP24}) For every $n\geq0$, $e_n(\mathbf{z})$ is a Drinfeld modular form of weight $q^n-1$. 
    
        \item (\cite[(15.1) and~(15.6)]{BBP24})  We have
        \[
        K[g_1,\ldots,g_{r-1},\Delta_r]
        =K[e_i\mid i\geq 1]=
        K[E_{q-1}^{(r)},\ldots,E_{q^r-1}^{(r)}].
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: lem:DMF-is-MES
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:DMF-is-MES}
    For any integer $r\geq 2$ and any subfield $L$ of $\mathbb{C}_\infty$ containing $K$, we have
    \[
    \mathscr{M}^{(r)}_L=L[g_1,\ldots,g_{r-1},\Delta_r]
    \subseteq
    \mathcal{Z}_{L}^{(r)}.
    \]
    Moreover, if
    $F\in L[g_1,\ldots,g_{r-1},\Delta_r]$
    is a Drinfeld modular form of weight $w$, then
    \[
    F\in \mathcal{Z}_{L,w}^{(r)}.
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq.single Eisenstein series of weight a}, for every
    $s\geq1$ with $q-1\mid s$, one checks that
    \[
    E_s^{(r)}(\mathbf{z})=-E_r(s;\mathbf{z}),
    \]
    and hence
    \[
    E_s^{(r)}\in\mathcal{Z}_{L,s}^{(r)}.
    \]
    
    By \cref{prop.ring of modular forms}, we have an equality of graded
    $L$-algebras
    \[
    L[g_1,\ldots,g_{r-1},\Delta_r]
    =
    L[E_{q-1}^{(r)},\ldots,E_{q^r-1}^{(r)}].
    \]
    Thus, if $F\in\mathscr{M}^{(r)}_{L,w}$, then $F$ is an $L$-linear
    combination of monomials in
    $E_{q-1}^{(r)},\ldots,E_{q^r-1}^{(r)}$ of total weight $w$.
    Since each $E_{q^i-1}^{(r)}$ belongs to
    $\mathcal{Z}_{L,q^i-1}^{(r)}$, it follows from \eqref{eq.q-shuffle-product-MES} that
    \[
    F\in\mathcal{Z}_{L,w}^{(r)}.
    \]
    The first assertion follows by summing over all weights.
head: environment

label: rmk:rank 1
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:rank 1}
We fix a $(q-1)$-st root of $(-\theta)$ and let
\[
\widetilde{\pi}
=
(-\theta)^{\frac{q}{q-1}}
\prod_{i=1}^{\infty}
\left(1-\frac{\theta}{\theta^{q^i}}\right)^{-1}
\in
K_{\infty}((-\theta)^{\frac{1}{q-1}})
\]
be a fixed fundamental period of the Carlitz $A$-module, namely,
$\phi_{\theta}^{\Lambda_{\widetilde{\pi}A}}=\theta+\tau$
(see \cite[\S3.2]{goss1996basic}). When $r=1$, we have the following.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The ``rank one discriminant form'' $\Delta_1$ is given by
    $\Delta_1=\widetilde{\pi}^{q-1}$ since the Drinfeld $A$-module $\phi^A$
    associated with the point $1\in\Omega^1$ is determined by
    \[
    \phi^A_\theta=\theta+\widetilde{\pi}^{q-1}\tau.
    \]
    By the Euler--Carlitz formula \cite{Car35} (see also \cite[Theorem~5.2.1]{thakur2004function}),
    $\Delta_1$ is a $K$-multiple of $\zeta_A(q-1)$. Hence
    \[
    \Delta_1^m\in\mathcal{Z}^{(1)}_{K,m(q-1)}
    \qquad (m\geq0),\qquad \text{and}\qquad
    L[\Delta_1]\subseteq\mathcal{Z}^{(1)}_L
    \]
    for any subfield $L$ of $\mathbb{C}_\infty$ containing $K$.

    \item For every $n\geq0$, the Carlitz exponential formula
    (see \cite[\S3.2]{goss1996basic}) gives
    \[
    e_n(1)
    =
    \frac{\widetilde{\pi}^{q^n-1}}{D_n}
    =
    \frac{1}{D_n}\Delta_1^{(q^n-1)/(q-1)}
    \in
    \mathcal{Z}^{(1)}_{K,q^n-1},
    \]
    where $D_0=1$ and $D_n = \prod_{j=0}^{n-1} (\theta^{q^n} - \theta^{q^j})$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: lem:coefficient-form-f
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:coefficient-form-f}
    Fix an integer $r\ge 1$ and denote by $\mathbf{w}$ an arbitrary point varying in $\Omega^r$.
    For $f\in A_+$ with $\deg f=d$, write
    \[
    \phi_f^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{w}}}(X)
    =
    \sum_{i=0}^{rd}g_{f,i}(\mathbf{w})X^{q^i}
    \in\mathcal{O}(\Omega^r)[X].
    \]
    Then
    \[
    g_{f,i}\in K[g_1,\ldots,g_{r-1},\Delta_r]
    \]
    is of weight $q^i-1$ for every $0\leq i\leq rd$. Moreover,
    \[
    g_{f,rd}
    =\Delta_r^{(q^{rd}-1)/(q^r-1)}.
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $r=1$, the assertions follow from \cref{rmk:rank 1} and the fact that
$\phi^A:A\to\mathbb{C}_\infty[\tau]$ is an $\mathbb{F}_q$-algebra homomorphism. For $r\geq 2$, see \cite[Propositions~15.12 and~16.4]{BBP24}.
head: environment

label: lem.t(fz)-coefficient
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem.t(fz)-coefficient}
    Fix an integer $r\ge 1$ and denote by $\mathbf{z} = (z_1, \mathbf{z}')$ an arbitrary point varying in $\Omega^{r+1}$.
    For $f\in A_+$, write
    \[
    t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(fz_1)=\sum_{N\geq 0}\mathcal{A}_{f,N}(\mathbf{z}')\cdot t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^N.
    \]
    Then 
    \[
    \mathcal{A}_{f,N}(\mathbf{z}')\in\mathcal{L}_{K,1-N}^{(r)}
    \]
    for all $N\geq 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $d=\deg f$. 
    We note that from~\eqref{eq.t-Lambda} and~\eqref{eq.exp linearity}, we have
    \begin{align*}
        t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(fz_1)
        &= \frac{1}{\exp_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(fz_1)}
        = \frac{1}{\phi_f^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}\left(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{-1}\right)} \\
        &= \frac{1}{\displaystyle\sum_{i=0}^{rd} g_{f,i}(\mathbf{z}')t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{-q^i}} \\
        &= \frac{t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{q^{rd}}}{g_{f,rd}(\mathbf{z}')} \left( 1+ \sum_{i=0}^{rd-1} \frac{g_{f,i}(\mathbf{z}')}{g_{f,rd}(\mathbf{z}')} t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{q^{rd}-q^i} \right)^{-1}.
    \end{align*}
    By \cref{lem:coefficient-form-f}, together with \cref{rmk:rank 1} for $r=1$ and \cref{lem:DMF-is-MES} for $r\geq2$, we have
    \[
    g_{f,i}(\mathbf{z}')\in\mathcal{Z}_{K,q^i-1}^{(r)},\qquad
    g_{f,rd}(\mathbf{z}')^{-1}\in\mathcal{L}_{K,1-q^{rd}}^{(r)},
    \]
    and hence
    \[
    \frac{g_{f,i}(\mathbf{z}')}{g_{f,rd}(\mathbf{z}')}
    \in
    \mathcal{L}^{(r)}_{K,q^i-q^{rd}}
    \qquad
    (0\leq i\leq rd-1).
    \]

    Expanding the inverse as a formal power series gives
    \[
    \left(
    1+
    \sum_{i=0}^{rd-1}
    \frac{g_{f,i}(\mathbf{z}')}{g_{f,rd}(\mathbf{z}')}
    t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{q^{rd}-q^i}
    \right)^{-1}
    =
    \sum_{m\geq0}
    (-1)^m
    \left(
    \sum_{i=0}^{rd-1}
    \frac{g_{f,i}(\mathbf{z}')}{g_{f,rd}(\mathbf{z}')}
    t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{q^{rd}-q^i}
    \right)^m.
    \]
    Consider a monomial occurring on the right-hand side,
    \[
    \prod_{j=1}^m
    \frac{g_{f,i_j}(\mathbf{z}')}{g_{f,rd}(\mathbf{z}')}\,
    t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{q^{rd}-q^{i_j}}.
    \]
    Its coefficient belongs to $\mathcal{L}_{K, \sum_{j=1}^m(q^{i_j}-q^{rd})}^{(r)},$ while its power of $t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)$ is
    \[
    \sum_{j=1}^m(q^{rd}-q^{i_j}).
    \]
    Thus, if such a monomial contributes to the coefficient of $t^N$
    in $t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(fz_1)$, then
    \[
    N = q^{rd} + \sum_{j=1}^m(q^{rd}-q^{i_j}),
    \]
    and its coefficient belongs to
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal{L}^{(r)}_{K, 1-q^{rd}
        +\sum_{j=1}^m(q^{i_j}-q^{rd})}
        &=
        \mathcal{L}_{K,1-N}^{(r)}.
    \end{align*}
    Therefore every term contributing to $\mathcal{A}_{f,N}(\mathbf{z}')$ lies in
    $\mathcal{L}^{(r)}_{K, 1-N}$, and hence
    \[
    \mathcal{A}_{f,N}(\mathbf{z}')\in\mathcal{L}_{K, 1-N}^{(r)}
    \]
    for all $N\geq0$.
head: environment

label: lem.Goss-poly-coefficient
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem.Goss-poly-coefficient}
    Fix an integer $r\ge 1$ and denote by $\mathbf{w}$ an arbitrary point varying in $\Omega^r$.
    For $s\geq 1$, write
    \[
    G_s^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{w}}}(X)=\sum_{i=1}^s \mathcal{B}_{s,i}(\mathbf{w})X^{i}\in\mathcal{O}(\Omega^r)[X].
    \]
    Then 
    \[
    \mathcal{B}_{s,i}\in\mathcal{L}_{K, s-i}^{(r)}
    \]
    for every $1\leq i\leq s$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that the coefficient $e_n(\mathbf{w}) \in \mathcal{O}(\Omega^r)$ of
    $\exp_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{w}}}(X)$ is defined in \eqref{eq.exponential coeff e_n}. By \cref{rmk:rank 1} for $r=1$ and \cref{prop.ring of modular forms,lem:DMF-is-MES} for $r\geq2$, we have
\[
e_n(\mathbf{w})\in\mathcal{Z}^{(r)}_{K,q^n-1}.
\]
    According to \cite[(3.8)]{Gekeler88}, the Goss polynomial
    associated with $\Lambda_{\mathbf{w}}$ is given by
    \[
    G_s^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{w}}}(X)
    =
    \sum_{j=0}^{s-1}\sum_{\underline{i}}
    \binom{j}{\underline{i}}
    \bm{e}^{\underline{i}}(\mathbf{w})X^{j+1},
    \]
    where the inner sum runs over all tuples
    $\underline{i}=(i_0,\ldots,i_{s-1})$ of non-negative integers satisfying
    \[
    \sum_{l=0}^{s-1} i_l=j
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \sum_{l=0}^{s-1} i_lq^l=s-1,
    \]
    and
    \[
    \bm{e}^{\underline{i}}(\mathbf{w})
    :=
    e_0(\mathbf{w})^{i_0}\cdots e_{s-1}(\mathbf{w})^{i_{s-1}}.
    \]
    Hence, by \eqref{eq.q-shuffle-product-MES},
    \[
    \bm{e}^{\underline{i}}(\mathbf{w})
    \in
    \mathcal{Z}^{(r)}_{K,\sum_{l=0}^{s-1} i_l(q^l-1)}
    =
    \mathcal{Z}^{(r)}_{K,s-1-j}.
    \]
    Taking $j=i-1$, we obtain
    \[
    \mathcal{B}_{s,i}(\mathbf{w})
    \in
    \mathcal{Z}^{(r)}_{K,s-i}
    \subseteq
    \mathcal{L}^{(r)}_{K,s-i}.
    \]
head: environment

label: lem:t-expansion of G(t(fz))
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:t-expansion of G(t(fz))}
    Fix an integer $r\ge 1$ and denote by $\mathbf{z} = (z_1, \mathbf{z}')$ an arbitrary point varying in $\Omega^{r+1}$.
    For $f\in A_+$ and $s\geq 1$, write
    \[
    G_s^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(fz_1))=\sum_{N\geq 0}\mathcal{C}_{s,f,N}(\mathbf{z}')\cdot t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{N}.
    \]
    Then 
    \[
    \mathcal{C}_{s,f,N}(\mathbf{z}')\in\mathcal{L}_{K, s-N}^{(r)}
    \]
    for all $N\geq 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Using the same notation as in \cref{lem.t(fz)-coefficient} and \cref{lem.Goss-poly-coefficient}, we see that
    \[
    G_s^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(fz_1)) = \sum_{i=1}^s \mathcal{B}_{s,i}(\mathbf{z}')\left(\sum_{M\geq 0}\mathcal{A}_{f,M}(\mathbf{z}')\cdot t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^M\right)^i
    \]
    Comparing the coefficient of $t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^N$, we obtain
    \begin{align*}
        \mathcal{C}_{s,f,N}(\mathbf{z}') &= \sum_{i=1}^s \mathcal{B}_{s,i}(\mathbf{z}') \left(\sum_{M_1 +\cdots + M_i = N}\prod_{j=1}^i  \mathcal{A}_{f,M_j}(\mathbf{z}')\right) \\
        &= \sum_{i=1}^s \sum_{M_1 +\cdots + M_i = N} \mathcal{B}_{s,i}(\mathbf{z}')\prod_{j=1}^i \mathcal{A}_{f,M_j}(\mathbf{z}').
    \end{align*}
    By \cref{lem.t(fz)-coefficient} and \cref{lem.Goss-poly-coefficient}, for each $1\le i \le s$, we have
    \[
    \mathcal{B}_{s,i}(\mathbf{z}')\prod_{j=1}^i  \mathcal{A}_{f,M_j}(\mathbf{z}') \in \mathcal{L}_{K, s-i}^{(r)} \cdot \mathcal{L}_{K, 1-M_1}^{(r)}\cdots \mathcal{L}_{K, 1-M_i}^{(r)} \subseteq\mathcal{L}_{K, s-N}^{(r)}. 
    \]
    Therefore, $\mathcal{C}_{s,f,N}(\mathbf{z}') \in \mathcal{L}_{K,s-N}^{(r)}$, as desired.
head: environment

label: prop:t-expansion of MGS
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:t-expansion of MGS}
    Fix an integer $r\ge 1$ and denote by $\mathbf{z} = (z_1, \mathbf{z}')$ an arbitrary point varying in $\Omega^{r+1}$.
    For any index $\mathfrak{s}$, write
    \[
    G_{r+1}(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z})=\sum_{N\geq 0}\alpha_{\mathfrak{s},N}(\mathbf{z}')\cdot t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{N}.
    \]
    Then 
    \[
    \alpha_{\mathfrak{s},N}(\mathbf{z}')\in\mathcal{L}_{K, \operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s})-N}^{(r)}
    \]
    for all $N\geq 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume that $\mathfrak{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)$ is nonempty. Fix $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A_+$ with $\deg f_1 > \cdots > \deg f_m$.
    Then by \cref{lem:t-expansion of G(t(fz))}, we have 
    \begin{align*}
        &G_{s_1}^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(f_1z_1))\cdots G_{s_m}^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(f_mz_1)) \\
        &= \left(\sum_{N_1=0}^{\infty}\mathcal{C}_{s_1,f_1,N_1}(\mathbf{z}')t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{N_1}\right)\cdots \left(\sum_{N_m=0}^{\infty}\mathcal{C}_{s_m,f_m,N_m}(\mathbf{z}')t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{N_m}\right) \\
        &= \sum_{N=0}^{\infty}\left(\sum_{\substack{N_1+\cdots+N_m=N \\ N_1,\ldots,N_m\ge 0}}\mathcal{C}_{s_1,f_1,N_1}(\mathbf{z}')\cdots \mathcal{C}_{s_m, f_m, N_m}(\mathbf{z}')\right)t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^N
    \end{align*}
    and 
    \[
    \mathcal{C}_{s_1,f_1,N_1}(\mathbf{z}')\cdots \mathcal{C}_{s_m,f_m,N_m}(\mathbf{z}')\in \mathcal{L}_{K, s_1-N_1}^{(r)}\cdots \mathcal{L}_{K, s_m-N_m}^{(r)} \subseteq \mathcal{L}_{K, \operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s})-N}^{(r)}.
    \]
    
    Now, note that by~\eqref{eq.ord_r(t(fz))}, for all $s\geq 1$ and $f\in A_+$, we have
    \[
    \operatorname{ord}_{r+1}(G_s(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(fz_1))) \ge q^{r\deg f}.
    \]
    In particular, if $\deg f > \frac{1}{r}\log_q (N+1)$, then $\operatorname{ord}_{r+1}(G_s(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(fz_1))) > N$.
    Hence, for all $N\geq 0$, 
    \begin{multline*}
        G_{r+1}(\mathfrak{s}; \mathbf{z}) \\
        \equiv \sum_{\substack{f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A_+ \\ \frac{1}{r}\log_q(N+1)\ge \deg f_1 > \cdots > \deg f_m}}G_{s_1}^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(f_1z_1))\cdots G_{s_m}^{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(f_mz_1)) 
        \pmod{t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{N+1}}.
    \end{multline*}
    Therefore, we obtain
    \[
    \alpha_{\mathfrak{s}, N}(\mathbf{z}') = \sum_{\substack{f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A_+ \\ \frac{1}{r}\log_q(N+1)\ge \deg f_1 > \cdots > \deg f_m}} \sum_{\substack{N_1+\cdots+N_m=N \\ N_1,\ldots, N_m\ge 0}}\mathcal{C}_{s_1,f_1,N_1}(\mathbf{z}')\cdots \mathcal{C}_{s_m, f_m, N_m}(\mathbf{z}')\in \mathcal{L}_{K,\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s}) - N}^{(r)}.
    \]

label: thm:t-expansion-of-MES
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:t-expansion-of-MES}
    Fix an integer $r\ge 1$ and denote by $\mathbf{z} = (z_1, \mathbf{z}')$ an arbitrary point varying in $\Omega^{r+1}$.
    For any index $\mathfrak{s}$, write
    \[
    E_{r+1}(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z})=\sum_{N\geq 0}\beta_{\mathfrak{s},N}(\mathbf{z}')\cdot t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^{N}.
    \]
    Then 
    \[
    \beta_{\mathfrak{s},N}(\mathbf{z}')\in\mathcal{L}^{(r)}_{K,\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s})-N}
    \]
    for all $N\geq 0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume that $\mathfrak{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)$ is nonempty.
    By \cref{prop.Goss expansion of MES}, we have
    \[
    E_{r+1}(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z})
    =
    \sum_{i=0}^{m}
    E_r(\mathfrak{s}^{(i)};\mathbf{z}')
    G_{r+1}(\mathfrak{s}_{(i)};\mathbf{z}).
    \]
    For each $0\leq i\leq m$, write
    \[
    G_{r+1}(\mathfrak{s}_{(i)};\mathbf{z})
    =
    \sum_{N\geq0}
    \alpha_{\mathfrak{s}_{(i)},N}(\mathbf{z}')
    t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^N.
    \]
    By \cref{prop:t-expansion of MGS}, we have
    \[
    \alpha_{\mathfrak{s}_{(i)},N}(\mathbf{z}')
    \in
    \mathcal{L}_{K,\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s}_{(i)})-N}^{(r)}.
    \]
    Moreover,
    \[
    E_r(\mathfrak{s}^{(i)};\mathbf{z}')
    \in
    \mathcal{Z}_{K,\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s}^{(i)})}^{(r)}
    \subseteq
    \mathcal{L}_{K,\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s}^{(i)})}^{(r)}.
    \]
    Hence
    \[
    E_r(\mathfrak{s}^{(i)};\mathbf{z}')
    \alpha_{\mathfrak{s}_{(i)},N}(\mathbf{z}')
    \in
    \mathcal{L}_{K,\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s})-N}^{(r)}.
    \]
    Comparing the coefficients of $t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)^N$, we obtain
    \[
    \beta_{\mathfrak{s},N}(\mathbf{z}')
    =
    \sum_{i=0}^{m}
    E_r(\mathfrak{s}^{(i)};\mathbf{z}')
    \alpha_{\mathfrak{s}_{(i)},N}(\mathbf{z}')
    \in
    \mathcal{L}_{K,\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s})-N}^{(r)},
    \]
    as desired.
head: environment

label: thm.main-thm over C_infty
title: Theorem
head: environment

label: cor.non-vanishing of MGS (rank 2)
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor.non-vanishing of MGS (rank 2)}
    For any index $\mathfrak{s}$, 
    \[
    G_2(\mathfrak{s}; \mathbf{z})\ne 0.
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $G_2(\mathfrak{s}; \mathbf{z}) = 0$, then 
    \[
    E_2(\mathfrak{s}; \mathbf{z}) = \sum_{i=0}^{\operatorname{dep}(\mathfrak{s})-1}\zeta_A(\mathfrak{s}^{(i)})G_2(\mathfrak{s}_{(i)}; \mathbf{z})\in \sum_{w=0}^{\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s})-1}\mathcal{Z}^{(2)}_{\mathbb{C}_{\infty}, w}.
    \]
    By \cref{thm.main-thm over C_infty}, this implies
\[
E_2(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf z)=0.
\]
On the other hand, by \cite[Proposition~2.10]{CCHT26}, the constant term
of the $t_{\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}}(z_1)$-expansion of $E_2(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf z)$ is
$E_1(\mathfrak{s})=\zeta_A(\mathfrak{s})$,
which is nonzero by \cite[Theorem~4]{Tha09}. This is a contradiction.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
For $\bm{f},\bm{g}\in A^r$, we define
    \[
    \bm{f}\succ_N0
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    \bm{f}\gamma_N\succ0,
    \]
    and
    \[
    \bm{f}\succ_N\bm{g}
    \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    \bm{f}\gamma_N\succ\bm{g}\gamma_N.
    \]
head: environment

label: lem:comparison between >_N and >
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\bm{f}=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. We have
    \[
    \bm{f}\gamma_N
    =
    (f_1,\ldots,f_{r-2},
    \theta^Nf_{r-1}+f_r,-f_{r-1}).
    \]
    If $\ell(\bm{f})\leq r-2$, the first nonzero coordinate of
    $\bm{f}\gamma_N$ is the same as that of $\bm{f}$, so the first
    assertion is immediate. If $\ell(\bm{f})=r-1$, then
    $\deg f_r<N$, while
    \[
    \deg(\theta^Nf_{r-1})
    =
    N+\deg f_{r-1}\geq N.
    \]
    Hence $\theta^Nf_{r-1}+f_r$ is monic if and only if
    $f_{r-1}$ is monic. Finally, if $\ell(\bm{f})=r$, then
    \[
    \bm{f}\gamma_N=(0,\ldots,0,f_r,0),
    \]
    so again $\bm{f}\succ_N0$ if and only if $\bm{f}\succ0$.
    This proves (i). The proof of (ii) follows from a similar argument.

label: df.shifted MES
title: Definition
head: environment

label: prop.shifted MES converges to MES
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop.shifted MES converges to MES}
    Let $\mathfrak{s}$ be an index.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item
        For every $\mathbf{z}\in\Omega^r$, there exists a constant
        $c(\mathbf{z})>0$ such that
        \[
        \left|
        E_r^{\langle N\rangle}(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z})
        -
        E_r(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z})
        \right|
        \leq
        c(\mathbf{z})q^{-N}
        \]
        for every $N\geq1$.
    
        \item
        For $\mathbf{z}=(z_1,\ldots,z_{r-1},1)\in\Omega^r$, put
        \[
        j_N(\mathbf{z})
        :=
        \theta^N-z_{r-1}.
        \]
        Then
        \[
        \mathbf{z}_N
        :=
        \left(
        \frac{z_1}{j_N(\mathbf{z})},
        \ldots,
        \frac{z_{r-2}}{j_N(\mathbf{z})},
        \frac{1}{j_N(\mathbf{z})},
        1
        \right)\in\Omega^r,
        \]
        and
        \[
        E_r(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z}_N)
        =
        j_N(\mathbf{z})^{\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s})}
        E_r^{\langle N\rangle}(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z}).
        \]
    \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that
    \[
    F_0+F_1+\cdots+F_w=0,
    \]
    where $F_i\in\mathcal{Z}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty,i}^{(r)}$ for every $0\leq i\leq w$.
    For each $i$, choose an expression
    \[
    F_i(\mathbf{z})
    =
    \sum_{j=1}^{m_i}
    c_{i,j}E_r(\mathfrak{s}_{i,j};\mathbf{z}),
    \]
    where $c_{i,j}\in\mathbb{C}_\infty$ and
    $\operatorname{wt}(\mathfrak{s}_{i,j})=i$, and put
    \[
    F_i^{\langle N \rangle}(\mathbf{z})
    :=
    \sum_{j=1}^{m_i}
    c_{i,j}E_r^{\langle N \rangle}(\mathfrak{s}_{i,j};\mathbf{z}).
    \]
    By \cref{prop.shifted MES converges to MES}, as $N\to\infty$,
    \[
    F_i^{\langle N \rangle}(\mathbf{z})\longrightarrow F_i(\mathbf{z}).
    \]
    
    Evaluating the given relation at $\mathbf{z}_N$ and applying
    \cref{prop.shifted MES converges to MES} again, we obtain
    \[
    0
    =
    \sum_{i=0}^{w}F_i(\mathbf{z}_N)
    =
    \sum_{i=0}^{w}
    j_N(\mathbf{z})^iF_i^{\langle N \rangle}(\mathbf{z}).
    \]
    Dividing by $j_N(\mathbf{z})^w$ yields
    \[
    F_w^{\langle N \rangle}(\mathbf{z})
    =
    -\sum_{i=0}^{w-1}
    j_N(\mathbf{z})^{i-w}F_i^{\langle N \rangle}(\mathbf{z}).
    \]
    Since $F_i^{\langle N \rangle}(\mathbf{z})\to F_i(\mathbf{z})$ as $N\to\infty$, the sequences
    $\{F_i^{\langle N \rangle}(\mathbf{z})\}_{N\geq1}$ are bounded. Moreover, for $N\gg0$,
    \[
    |j_N(\mathbf{z})|^{-1}
    =
    |\theta^N-z_{r-1}|^{-1}
    =
    q^{-N}\longrightarrow0.
    \]
    Hence, letting $N\to\infty$ in the preceding identity yields
    \[
    F_w(\mathbf{z})=0.
    \]
    Repeating the same argument for
    $F_0+\cdots+F_{w-1}=0$, we obtain
    \[
    F_0=F_1=\cdots=F_w=0.
    \]
    Therefore,
    \[
    \mathcal{Z}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty}^{(r)}
    =
    \bigoplus_{w\geq0}\mathcal{Z}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty,w}^{(r)}.
    \]
head: environment

label: prop.Gcal is defined over K
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Notice that for any $\mathbf{z}\in \Omega^2$, $\Lambda_{\mathbf{z}'}=A$. Let $C=\phi^{\widetilde{\pi}A}$ denote the Carlitz $A$-module and $\exp_C(X)=\exp_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(X)\in K[\![X]\!]$ denote the Carlitz exponential (see \cite[\S3]{goss1996basic}). 
    By \cref{df.Goss polynomial,prop.G_a(t(X)) = sum 1/(X+λ)^a}, we have
    \[
    G_s^{\widetilde{\pi}A}(X)\in K[X]
    \qquad
    (s\geq1),\qquad\text{and}\qquad
    G_s^{\widetilde{\pi}A}
    \bigl(t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}fz_1)\bigr)
    =
    \widetilde{\pi}^{-s}
    G_s^A\bigl(t_A(fz_1)\bigr).
    \]
    On the other hand, for every $f\in A_+$, we have
    \[
    t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}fz_1)
    =
    \frac{1}{\exp_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}fz_1)}
    =
    \frac{1}{C_f(\exp_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}z_1))}
    =
    \frac{1}{
    C_f\bigl(t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}z_1)^{-1}\bigr)
    }\in
    K[\![t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}z_1)]\!].
    \]
    It follows that for every nonempty index
    $\mathfrak{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)$,
    \[
    \widetilde{G}_2(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z})= \sum_{\substack{f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A_+ \\ \deg f_1 > \cdots > \deg f_m}}G_{s_1}^{\widetilde{\pi}A}(t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}f_1z_1))\cdots G_{s_m}^{\widetilde{\pi}A}(t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}f_mz_1))
    \in
    K[\![t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}z_1)]\!].
    \]
    Here, for each $M\geq 0$, \eqref{eq.ord_r(t(fz))} shows that only finitely many terms in the series above contribute to its $t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}z_1)^M$-coefficient. Hence this coefficient belongs to $K$.
    Therefore, we get an injective $K$-linear map
    \[
    \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{K,\le w}^{(2)}\hookrightarrow K[\![t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}z_1)]\!].
    \]
    Since $\mathbb{C}_\infty$ is flat over $K$, 
    \[
    \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{K,\le w}^{(2)}\otimes_K \mathbb{C}_{\infty}\hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}_{\infty}[\![t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}z_1)]\!]
    \]
    is still an injection.
    Notice that the image $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{K,\le w}^{(2)}\otimes_K \mathbb{C}_{\infty}\to \mathbb{C}_{\infty}[\![t_{\widetilde{\pi}A}(\widetilde{\pi}z_1)]\!]$ is $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{\mathbb{C}_{\infty},\le w}$, so the assertion follows.
head: environment

label: prop. MES iso to gr MGS
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop. MES iso to gr MGS}
    Let $L = K$ or $\mathbb{C}_\infty$.
    Then for any integer $w\ge 0$ the map 
    \[
    \varphi_{L,w}:=\left(\widetilde{E}_2(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z}) \mapsto \widetilde{G}_2(\mathfrak{s};\mathbf{z}) \mod{\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{L,\le w-1}^{(2)}} \right) : \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{L,w}^{(2)} \to \operatorname{gr}_w\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{L}^{(2)}.
    \] 
    is a well-defined isomorphism.
head: environment
labels: prop. MES iso to gr MGS

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume $w\geq1$ as the case $w=0$ is clear.
    We first show the well-definedness for $L = \mathbb{C}_{\infty}$.
    Suppose
    \[
    0 = \sum_{i=1}^{m} c_i\widetilde{E}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z}) \in \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty,w}^{(2)}
    \]
    for some $c_i\in \mathbb{C}_\infty$.
    Then by~\eqref{eq.normalized MES Goss expansion} we have
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^{m} c_i\widetilde{G}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z}) = -\sum_{i=1}^{m} c_i \sum_{j=0}^{\operatorname{dep}(\mathfrak{s}_i)-1} \widetilde{\zeta}_A((\mathfrak{s}_i)^{(j)})\widetilde{G}_2((\mathfrak{s}_i)_{(j)}) \in \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}^{(2)}_{\mathbb{C}_{\infty}, \le w-1}.
    \]
    Hence, $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}_{\infty}, w}$ is well-defined.
    
    Now, we show the well-definedness for $L=K$. Suppose that 
    \[
    0 = \sum_{i=1}^{m} c_i\widetilde{E}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z}) \in \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{K,w}^{(2)}
    \]
    for some $c_i\in K$.
    Similarly, by~\eqref{eq.normalized MES Goss expansion} and~\eqref{eq.intersection property}, we see that
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i\widetilde{G}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z})\in \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}^{(2)}_{K, \le w}\cap \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}^{(2)}_{\mathbb{C}_{\infty}, \le w-1} = \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}^{(2)}_{K, \le w-1}
    \]
    Hence, $\varphi_{K, w}$ is well-defined.

    For $L=K$ or $L=\mathbb{C}_{\infty}$, we note that the surjectivity of $\varphi_{L,w}$ is clear from the definition.
    We then show the injectivity of $\varphi_{L, w}$ as follows.
    Suppose that $\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i\widetilde{E}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z})\in \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}^{(2)}_{L, w}$ such that 
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i\widetilde{G}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z}) \in \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}^{(2)}_{L, \le w-1}\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}^{(2)}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty, \le w-1}.
    \]
    By~\eqref{eq.normalized MES Goss expansion}, we have
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i\widetilde{E}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z}) -\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i\widetilde{G}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z}) \in \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}^{(2)}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty, \le w-1},
    \]
    which implies
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i\widetilde{E}_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z})\in \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}^{(2)}_{\mathbb{C}_{\infty}, \le w-1} \subseteq \sum_{j=0}^{w-1}\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}^{(2)}_{\mathbb{C}_{\infty}, j}.
    \]
    Therefore, by~\cref{thm.main-thm over C_infty}~(i), we obtain
    \[
    \sum_{i=1}^{m}c_iE_2(\mathfrak{s}_i; \mathbf{z})\in \sum_{j=0}^{w-1}\mathcal{Z}^{(2)}_{\mathbb{C}_{\infty}, j} \cap \mathcal{Z}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty,w}^{(2)} = 0.
    \]
    This proves the injectivity.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to show the case $r=2$.
    For general $r\geq 2$, the result follows by adapting the induction argument of~\cref{thm.main-thm}~(ii), with $\overline{K}$ replaced by $\mathbb{C}_\infty$ and the base case of the induction replaced by the case $r=2$.
    
    Assume $r=2$ and $w\ge 1$.
    The map $\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{K,w}^{(2)}\otimes_K \mathbb{C}_\infty \to \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty,w}^{(2)}$ fits into the following commutative diagram:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
    {\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{K,w}^{(2)}\otimes_K \mathbb{C}_\infty}
    &
    {\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty,w}^{(2)}}
    \\
    {\operatorname{gr}_w\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_K^{(2)}\otimes_K \mathbb{C}_\infty}
    &
    {\operatorname{gr}_w\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty}^{(2)}}
    \arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
    \arrow["\sim", sloped, from=1-1, to=2-1]
    \arrow["\sim"', sloped, from=1-2, to=2-2]
    \arrow["\sim", from=2-1, to=2-2]
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where the three isomorphisms follow from \cref{prop. MES iso to gr MGS} and~\eqref{eq. gr define over K}.
    This implies $\widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{K,w}^{(2)}\otimes_K \mathbb{C}_\infty \xrightarrow{\sim} \widetilde{\mathcal{Z}}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty,w}^{(2)}$ is an isomorphism.
    Therefore, by~\eqref{eq. isom of nonnormalized and normalized MES}, we obtain
    \[
    \mathcal{Z}_{K,w}^{(2)}\otimes_K \mathbb{C}_\infty \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{Z}_{\mathbb{C}_\infty,w}^{(2)}.
    \]
    The assertion for $r=2$ follows from summing over all $w\ge 0$.
    This completes the proof.
